description: We are a team of 6 students with backgrounds in Cybersecurity, AI, and Software Development. For NASA Space Apps, we’re tackling “Flame in Freefall” by combining AI, data analysis, and software engineering to understand fire behavior in microgravity and extract meaningful fire-safety insights. We bring together technical, research, and problem-solving skills to build an innovative solution. 🔥🚀
summary:
FLARE AI (Fire & Low-Gravity Archive Research Engine) is a source-grounded scientific decision-support platform built on NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archive to address the "Flame in Freefall" challenge. In microgravity, flames lack buoyant convection—burning as spherical, diffusion-driven fronts that can persist at lower oxygen levels and produce larger smoke particles than on Earth. However, historical NASA spaceflight combustion experiments span heterogeneous formats, units, combustion domains, and unrecorded environmental variables.

FLARE AI unifies 1,157 experiment runs, 10,079 measurements, 128 verified archive files, and 1,312 scientific document passages across six NASA PSI investigations (FLEX, BASS-II, SPICE, SAME, SAME-R, and Saffire-I). It combines a domain-gated, confidence-penalized similarity ranking engine with a guardrail-enforced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) assistant that verifies every citation quote verbatim and explicitly flags missing parameters and partial-gravity (Lunar/Martian) archive gaps—accelerating spacecraft fire-safety research without hallucinating or extrapolating beyond physical bounds.
details:
What FLARE AI Does & How It Works

FLARE AI is a hybrid scientific knowledge and decision-support platform designed for researchers studying spacecraft fire behavior across NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) archive. Rather than acting as a black-box chatbot or claiming to predict ignition risk, FLARE AI operates through three tightly integrated, provenance-auditable layers:

  1. Standardized Multi-Investigation Data Pipeline & Provenance Registry (FLARE_AI_Data_Handoff)
  • Ingests, normalizes, and cross-checks 6 NASA PSI investigations (PSI-69 FLEX, PSI-25 BASS-II, PSI-107 SPICE, PSI-101 SAME-R, PSI-102 SAME, and PSI-98 Saffire-I), encompassing 1,157 experiment runs, 10,079 measurements, 128 SHA-256-verified raw files, 33 coverage/gap matrix cells (COV-/GAP-), and 1,312 chunked passages from 21 NASA technical reports and peer-reviewed publications.
  • Preserves both raw reported units (e.g., mmHg, % vol, instrument fan settings) and canonical normalized units (kPa, O2 mole fraction, cm/s), while enforcing explicit missingness categories (not_reported, not_measured, not_applicable, pending_review) instead of imputing missing values.
  1. Domain-Gated, Confidence-Penalized Similarity Ranking Engine (flare_ranking)
  • Ranks historical NASA experiment runs against a researcher's target environmental conditions (O2 fraction, ambient pressure in kPa, forced airflow velocity in cm/s, combustion domain, and gravity regime).
  • Hard Domain Gating: Prevents invalid cross-domain comparisons (solid fuels in BASS-II/Saffire-I are never numerically ranked against liquid droplets in FLEX, gas jets in SPICE, or smoke aerosols in SAME/SAME-R).
  • Gravity Regime Separation: Separates ISS/Cygnus microgravity (0g) runs from normal-gravity (1g) ground baselines and flags partial-gravity (0.16g Lunar / 0.38g Martian) queries as open archive gaps bounded by 0g and 1g.
  • Confidence Penalty: Separates condition similarity (S_cond) from data completeness (C_conf) so experiments with missing parameters cannot artificially outrank fully measured runs.
  1. Guardrail-Enforced Scientific RAG Copilot (flare_llm_engine & flare_llm_adapter)
  • Retrieves relevant NASA PSI document chunks and coverage-matrix cells (COV-/GAP-) via hybrid semantic + lexical + structured SQL retrieval.
  • Enforces strict scientific guardrails (G1–G7 and D1–D6): never claims to predict fire risk or certify astronaut safety, never interpolates partial-gravity behavior between 0g and 1g, and verifies every LLM citation quote character-for-character against the underlying source passage (verified: true).

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Eliminates Data Silos Across Spaceflight Fire Experiments: Unifies droplet extinction, solid flame spread, gas-jet smoke points, and spacecraft smoke detector aerosol distributions into one searchable, unit-harmonized schema.
  • Prevents Dangerous Scientific Extrapolation: Automatically warns researchers when target conditions fall into untested partial-gravity regimes (Moon/Mars) or when source experiments lack ambient O2/pressure logs (such as SPICE, SAME, and SAME-R).
  • Full Auditability to Primary DOIs: Every run, measurement, and AI-synthesized statement links directly to its NASA PSI investigation, DOI, and SHA-256 source file checksum.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Backend & Data Engineering: Python 3, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic v2, NumPy, Pandas, SQLite / PostgreSQL, HTTPX.
  • Similarity & Ranking Engine: Custom Python weighted min-max similarity and confidence-penalty engine (flare_ranking) with pytest verification suites.
  • AI / RAG & Guardrail Engine: Google Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash) / OpenAI (gpt-4o) structured JSON outputs with deterministic citation verification (flare_llm_engine.py) and hybrid vector + lexical + SQL retrieval.
  • Frontend UI: Next.js 15 (React 19, TypeScript), Tailwind CSS, KaTeX scientific math rendering, interactive condition comparison sliders, and a slide-over Provenance & Lineage Inspector.

How Our Project Is Creative & Factors Considered

  • Honest Uncertainty Over Hallucination: Most AI tools guess when data is missing. FLARE AI treats missingness (not_reported, pending_review) and archive gaps (GAP-* cells) as first-class scientific data.
  • Physics-Aware Architecture: Our team accounted for real spacecraft hardware quirks—such as BASS-II nitrogen-dilution schedules, SPICE/BASS-II fan calibration curves, and SAME/SAME-R mixed ISS (0g) vs. ground (1g) baseline runs—ensuring physical fidelity at every step.https://flame-ai-six.vercel.app/explorer
